subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be limited to diagnostics for blocked Telegram `MEDIA:` paths while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns root expansion, or should this issue define a new host-local outbound media root contract too?
rationale: The diagnostic fix is narrow, but accepting more host-local paths or adding a root config key changes which files OpenClaw may read and upload through channel delivery.

options.title: Diagnostics here, roots in the canonical policy issue
options.body: Keep this item for warn-level reasoned drops and optional unavailable-attachment UX, while the open configurable-root issue owns the security-reviewed root contract.

options.title: Make this the root-policy owner
options.body: Use this item to define a supported Telegram or shared outbound media-root config surface, with schema, docs, tests, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Document managed roots only
options.body: Decline new root expansion and close the policy portion after documenting managed roots, staging directories, and the message-tool workaround.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, roots in the canonical policy issue
recommendation.body: Keep this item for warn-level reasoned drops and optional unavailable-attachment UX, while the open configurable-root issue owns the security-reviewed root contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest recent history on outbound media policy and the host-read boundary that the decision would change.
